title: Chasing the Olive Crown: Inside the Ancient Olympic Games
title_zh: 追寻橄榄枝桂冠：古代奥林匹克运动会探秘
intro_zh: 本文约900词，介绍古代奥运会的起源、比赛项目、规则和文化意义，适合CET-4水平阅读。

paragraphs.en: Every four years, the world comes together for the modern Olympic Games, which feature thousands of athletes from over two hundred countries. However, few people realize that this global event traces its roots back to a small Greek town nearly 3,000 years ago. The ancient Olympic Games, held in Olympia, were quite different from today's competitions. They were not merely sports contests; they were religious celebrations dedicated to Zeus, the king of the Greek gods. For more than one thousand years, the games served as a unifying force for Greek city-states, which often fought each other. During the duration of the games, a sacred truce was proclaimed, so that athletes, travelers, and spectators could journey safely through enemy territory. This custom was so important that any city violating the truce faced heavy fines.
paragraphs.zh: 每四年，全世界都会聚集起来庆祝现代奥运会，这场盛事有来自200多个国家的数千名运动员参加。然而，很少有人意识到，这一全球性活动可以追溯到近3000年前的一个希腊小城镇。古代奥运会在奥林匹亚举行，与现代的竞赛大不相同。它们不仅仅是体育竞赛，更是献给希腊众神之王宙斯的宗教庆典。一千多年来，这些运动会成为了经常相互争斗的希腊城邦的团结力量。在运动会期间，会宣布神圣休战，使运动员、旅行者和观众能够安全地穿越敌方领土。这一习俗非常重要，任何破坏休战的城邦都会面临重罚。

paragraphs.en: The exact origin of the ancient Olympics is surrounded by myth and legend. One popular story recounts that the hero Hercules, the son of Zeus, established the games in honor of his father after completing his famous twelve labors. Another legend involves a mythical king named Oenomaus, who challenged suitors to a chariot race. The historical record points to 776 BC, when the first recorded Olympic champion, a cook named Coroebus, won the sole event: a short footrace called the 'stadion'. The length of the race was exactly 192 meters, which is the length of the stadium at Olympia. In those early days, the games lasted only a single day. But as more events were added, the festival expanded to five days, allowing more time for competitions and religious ceremonies.
paragraphs.zh: 古代奥运会的确切起源笼罩在神话和传说之中。一个流行的故事讲述了英雄赫拉克勒斯在完成十二项功绩后，为了纪念他的父亲宙斯而创立了奥运会。另一个传说涉及一位名叫欧诺玛俄斯的国王，他挑战求婚者进行战车比赛。历史记录指向公元前776年，当时第一位有记录的奥运会冠军——一位名叫科罗伊博斯的厨师——赢得了唯一一个项目：名为“斯塔迪昂”的短跑。比赛距离正好是192米，也就是奥林匹亚体育场的长度。在早期，运动会只持续一天。但随着项目的增多，庆典延长到五天，为比赛和宗教仪式留出了更多时间。

paragraphs.en: Over the centuries, the Olympic program grew steadily. In 724 BC, a two-length race was introduced, and shortly after came wrestling and boxing. By the seventh century BC, the pentathlon was a highlight, featuring running, jumping, discus, javelin, and wrestling. Chariot racing, a thrilling and dangerous event, was added around 680 BC. Owners of the horses were credited with victory, not the riders, so wealthy Greeks often hired professional charioteers. These sports demanded intense physical skill and courage. Spectators could number up to fifty thousand, packing the hillsides around the stadium to cheer for their hometown heroes. Unlike today's Olympics, there were no gold, silver, or bronze medals. The sole prize for each winner was a crown woven from wild olive leaves, cut from a sacred tree with a golden knife.
paragraphs.zh: 几个世纪以来，奥运会的项目稳步增加。公元前724年，引入了双程跑，不久后又出现了摔跤和拳击。到了公元前七世纪，五项全能成为亮点，包括赛跑、跳远、铁饼、标枪和摔跤。战车赛跑大约在公元前680年被加入，这是一项刺激而危险的运动。马匹的主人被记作胜利者，而不是骑手，因此富有的希腊人常常雇佣职业战车驭手。这些运动要求极强的身体技能和勇气。观众人数可多达五万人，他们挤满体育场周围的山坡，为自己的家乡英雄加油。与现代奥运会不同的是，这里没有金牌、银牌或铜牌。每位胜利者唯一的奖品是用野生橄榄枝编织的花冠，是从一棵圣树上用金刀割下的。

paragraphs.en: In ancient Greece, participation in the Olympics was restricted to free-born Greek men. Women were banned from competing, and married women were even prohibited from watching the games, though young girls and priestesses could attend. Athletes had to undergo ten months of rigorous training before the games, following a strict diet that included figs, cheese, and meat. The ancient gymnasium was a center for preparation, equipped with oil jars and scrapers. During events, athletes competed in the nude, a unique custom that fascinated later historians. The Greeks believed this practice honored the gods and displayed the ideal of athletic beauty. A famous quote attributed to the philosopher Socrates urges: 'No one enters the Olympics to win merely for money; they seek glory and honor.'
paragraphs.zh: 在古希腊，参加奥运会仅限于自由出生的希腊男性。女性被禁止参赛，已婚妇女甚至被禁止观看比赛，不过年轻女孩和女祭司可以出席。运动员必须在比赛前接受十个月的严格训练，遵守包括无花果、奶酪和肉类在内的严格饮食。古代体育馆是训练的中心，配备有油罐和刮身板。在比赛中，运动员全裸参赛，这是一个让后世历史学家着迷的独特习俗。希腊人相信这种做法能取悦众神，并展示运动之美。著名的哲学家苏格拉底有句名言：“没有人为了钱而进入奥运会；他们追求的是荣耀和荣誉。”

paragraphs.en: Fairness was paramount at the ancient Games. Judges, known as Hellanodikai, were chosen from noble families and sworn to be impartial. They had the authority to whip cheaters or exclude them from the games. The competitors swore an oath to obey the rules. If an athlete paid an opponent to lose, all parties involved could be heavily fined, and the money was used to build bronze statues of Zeus, called Zanes. The reward for a champion may have appeared modest: an olive crown and a palm branch. But the glory that accompanied this victory was enormous. Winners became heroes in their hometowns, receiving free meals, front-row seats at the theater, and sometimes larger-than-life statues. In some city-states, they were even exempt from taxes.
paragraphs.zh: 公平在古代奥运会上至关重要。裁判被称为“赫拉尼奥迪凯”，从贵族家族中选出，并发誓公正无私。他们有权鞭打作弊者或将其逐出比赛。参赛者宣誓遵守规则。如果运动员收买对手输掉比赛，所有相关方都可能被重罚，罚款用于铸造宙斯青铜像，称为“扎内斯”。对冠军的奖励可能看起来微不足道：一个橄榄花冠和一根棕榈枝。但这种胜利带来的荣耀是巨大的。胜利者成为家乡的英雄，享有终身免费餐、剧场前排座位，有时还有真人大小以上的雕像。在某些城邦，他们甚至免征赋税。

paragraphs.en: The Olympic Games were far more than athletic events; they were a sacred ritual for the Greeks. At the heart of Olympia stood the Temple of Zeus, which housed a magnificent gold-and-ivory statue of the god, almost 12 meters high, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. During the festival, athletes made sacrifices to Zeus, often offering small animals. The altars were covered with gifts from thank-offerings. Beyond sports, poets, musicians, and philosophers flocked to Olympia to perform and exchange ideas. Herodotus, the 'father of history,' read his works there. This blend of sport, religion, and culture made the games a unifying tradition for the entire Greek-speaking world. The lighting of a flame in front of the temple was a central part of the ceremony.
paragraphs.zh: 奥运会远不止是体育赛事；对希腊人来说，它是一种神圣的仪式。奥林匹亚的中心矗立着宙斯神庙，里面供奉着一尊几乎12米高的巨型宙斯神像，由黄金和象牙制成，是古代世界七大奇迹之一。在节日期间，运动员向宙斯献祭，通常供奉小动物。圣坛上堆满了感恩祭品。在体育之外，诗人、音乐家和哲学家纷纷涌向奥林匹亚表演和交流思想。历史之父希罗多德在那里朗读过他的作品。这种体育、宗教和文化的融合使运动会成为整个希腊世界统一传统的盛事。在神庙前点燃火焰的仪式是庆典的核心部分。

paragraphs.en: The ancient Olympics endured for nearly 1,200 years, surviving political turmoil and cultural change. However, when the Roman Empire took over Greece, the games began to alter. Roman emperors sometimes forced athletes to compete against wild animals for spectacles, and the religious significance gradually faded. By the late fourth century AD, the Christian emperor Theodosius I, wishing to stamp out pagan traditions, issued an edict in 393 AD that banned all such festivals. The great Temple of Zeus was closed, and the site was eventually abandoned. Over time, earthquakes and floods covered the ruins with earth, and the memory of the ancient Games slipped into obscurity for nearly 1,500 years.
paragraphs.zh: 古代奥运会持续了近1200年，历经政治动荡和文化变迁。然而，当罗马帝国接管希腊时，运动会开始发生变化。罗马皇帝有时强迫运动员与野兽搏斗以取乐，宗教意义逐渐褪色。到公元四世纪末，基督教皇帝狄奥多西一世为了根除异教传统，于公元393年颁布法令，禁止所有此类节日。宙斯神庙被关闭，遗址最终被废弃。随着时间的推移，地震和洪水用泥土覆盖了废墟，古代奥运会的记忆在近1500年里渐渐被人遗忘。

paragraphs.en: The ancient Games were rediscovered through archaeology in the nineteenth century. In 1875, German archaeologists began excavating the site of Olympia, uncovering temples and stadiums. Inspired by these discoveries, French educator Baron Pierre de Coubertin worked to revive the Olympics. He founded the International Olympic Committee, and the first modern Games were held in Athens in 1896. Many traditions we see today, such as the Olympic flame and the torch relay, are directly inspired by ancient rituals. The Olympic motto 'Faster, Higher, Stronger' originally came from a French priest and reflects the endless pursuit of human excellence. The modern Olympics, although global, still pays tribute to the ancient Greek legacy of fair competition.
paragraphs.zh: 古代运动会通过19世纪的考古学重新被发现。1875年，德国考古学家开始发掘奥林匹亚遗址，出土了神庙和体育场。受到这些发现的启发，法国教育家皮埃尔·德·顾拜旦努力复兴奥运会。他成立了国际奥委会，第一届现代奥运会于1896年在雅典举行。我们今天看到的许多传统，如奥运圣火和火炬传递，都直接受到古代仪式的启发。奥运格言“更快、更高、更强”最初来自一位法国神父，它反映了对人类卓越的无尽追求。现代奥运会虽然全球化，却仍然向古代希腊公平竞争的传统致敬。

paragraphs.en: The Olympic Games of antiquity were not just a series of athletic competitions. They were a powerful expression of unity, faith, and human ambition. The games taught that even in times of war, rivals could come together under a truce and celebrate excellence. The olive crown may be a modest symbol, but it carried the dreams of every Greek athlete. Today, as we watch athletes from all around the world raise their own flags, we can still hear the echoes of those ancient runners on the dusty track of Olympia. The spirit of the ancient Games lives on, reminding us that humanity's greatest victories are not only measured by speed or strength, but by the courage and honor we bring to the contest.
paragraphs.zh: 古代奥运会不仅仅是一系列体育比赛。它们是团结、信仰和人类雄心的有力表达。运动会告诉我们，即使在战争时期，对手也能在休战下走到一起，赞美卓越。橄榄花冠可能是一个朴素的象征，但它承载着每一位希腊运动员的梦想。今天，当我们看到来自世界各地的运动员举起自己的旗帜时，我们仍然能听到古代跑者留在奥林匹亚尘土跑道上的回声。古代奥运会的精神永存，它提醒我们，人类最大的胜利不仅以速度或力量来衡量，更以我们在竞赛中带来的勇气和荣誉来衡量。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The ancient Olympic Games were purely religious events.
The ancient Olympic Games were quite different from modern ones and left a lasting legacy.
The ancient Olympic Games were only for men in Greece.
The ancient Olympic Games were cancelled by Roman emperors.
questions.explain: 文章主要介绍了古代奥运会的起源、特点、发展及对现代的影响，因此B正确。A过于绝对，C不全面，D只是其中一部分。

questions.q: According to the passage, which event was part of the ancient pentathlon?
questions.explain: 根据第三段，五项全能包括赛跑、跳远、铁饼、标枪和摔跤，因此C（铁饼）正确。

questions.q: Why were married women not allowed to watch the ancient Olympics?
options: Because they were too busy with household duties.
Because the athletes competed naked and the Greeks wanted to keep the games pure.
Because they had to stay at home to prepare sacrifices.
Because the stadium was too crowded.
questions.explain: 第四段提到运动员全裸参赛，且已婚妇女被禁止观看，结合古希腊习俗，可以推断这与裸体有关，因此B最合理。

questions.q: The word 'truce' in Paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to?
questions.explain: 根据上下文，神圣休战是让敌对城邦在奥运会期间停止战斗，因此truce意为‘停战协定’，选B。
